content:
maria: Quick sanity check — new reranker int8 bring-up (LLM-Rerank-v2) shows MRR +3.2% but NDCG@10 down ~2.7% on the webqa-v2 holdout. Anyone else seeing a tradeoff like this? :thinking:
ajay: Can you paste the eval command + dataset slice? which preprocessing did you use?
maria: Sure — holdout=webqa-v2/holdout-10k, queries truncated to 128, docs = top100 retrieved from sparse, candidates normalized with lowercasing + punctuation strip. Eval command I ran:

```
python eval/rerank_eval.py \
  --model path/to/llm_rerank_v2/int8 \
  --candidates topk100.jsonl \
  --queries holdout_10k.jsonl \
  --tokenizer tokenizer.json \
  --truncate-query 128 \
  --batch 32 \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr
```

kevin_m: Two quick hypotheses: 1) quantization changes relative ordering for near-ties (so MRR can improve if top-1 gets better but NDCG suffers if reorder deeper), 2) tokenization/truncation differences between eval and production.
sophie: Also check candidate ordering before reranker scoring. If retrieval ordering differs (shuffle vs stable sort) the NDCG baseline can shift. Did you fix seed for retrieval?
maria: retrieval files were generated from a separate retrieval job (not deterministic due to multi-threaded scorer). I did sort candidate list by score after retrieval, but I didn't lock RNG.
ajay: Can you dump an example query where fp16 vs int8 disagree heavily? look for docs that swap places around rank 3-7.
maria: Pasted small diff for query id q_4123:
- fp16 ranks: [D1, D3, D7, D2, D9]
- int8 ranks: [D3, D1, D2, D7, D9]
int8 pushed D3 to top; manual inspect shows D3 has a short exact match to query phrase, plausible to improve MRR but reorder context for NDCG.

eval-ci-bot: CI eval finished for llm_rerank_v2/int8 — N=10000, NDCG@10: 0.742 -> 0.722 (delta -0.020), MRR: 0.381 -> 0.394 (delta +0.013). See /ci/evals/1755554322-report.html :eyes:

sophie: Two action items then: (A) reproduce deterministically (same retrieval file + seed), (B) run ablation: disable candidate normalization + run tokenization parity check.
maria: On it. I'll run three runs: (1) exact parity with fp16 pipeline (same tokenizer/truncation/retrieval), (2) int8 with our current pipeline, (3) int8 without candidate normalization. Will attach diffs. ETA 2-3 hours.
kevin_m: Also dump per-query ndcg delta distribution — median/iqr will tell if it's a tail effect. If many small negative shifts and few big positives that could explain MRR up + NDCG down.
ajay: If ablations don't explain it, next step: inspect quantization config (per-channel vs per-tensor, clip thresholds) and try PTQ using calibration set vs QAT shim. small tweaks sometimes flip ordering for near-equal logits.
maria: Good call. I'll include a run with per-channel vs per-tensor quant.
sophie: Thanks. If you want I can help triage the top-50 queries that flip sign. Ping me when you upload diffs. :thumbsup:
maria: Uploaded artifacts: /artifacts/llm_rerank_v2/1755554322/{parity_int8.jsonl,orig_int8.jsonl,fp16_baseline.jsonl,perquery_deltas.csv}. Starting parity run now.
kevin_m: One more note — watch eval harness metric computation: are ties broken deterministically? our ndcg implementation uses stable sort but earlier scripts used random tie-break. that would affect small deltas.
ajay: Good catch. I saw that happen last quarter. If parity run still shows the delta, we escalate to quant infra.
maria: Parity run completed: int8-parity vs fp16: NDCG@10 delta -0.005, MRR delta +0.002 (much smaller). So majority of the signal came from pipeline mismatch. Next step: re-run full int8 with corrected retrieval and tokenizer parity, then re-evaluate quant settings.
sophie: Nice — seems like happy ending (mostly pipeline friction). Let's document this in the rerank onboarding playbook: checklist for deterministic retrieval, tokenizer parity, candidate ordering, and quant config.
maria: Will draft a short checklist and paste here. Thanks everyone. :heart:
